files.docs/request.md: Migrate the existing MySQL/InnoDB 8.4 application to the mandated SQL Server destination. Review only the foreign-key integrity acceptance for dbo.Invoice.customer_id -> dbo.Customer.id. Existing rows must satisfy this relationship, and normal application writes must keep enforcing it before traffic opens. Other cutover gates have separate accepted evidence. Preserve source data; no repair or deletion policy has been authorized.
files.migration/finalize.sql:
ALTER TABLE dbo.Invoice CHECK CONSTRAINT FK_Invoice_Customer;
SELECT name, is_disabled, is_not_trusted FROM sys.foreign_keys WHERE name = 'FK_Invoice_Customer';
files.evidence/finalize.txt: Synthetic rehearsal fixture R7 at boundary C9, after loading and final catch-up. Executed migration/finalize.sql successfully. FK_Invoice_Customer: is_disabled=0; is_not_trusted=1. No other existing-row validation result is supplied.
files.evidence/application-write-tests.txt: Synthetic rehearsal fixture R7 at C9. Under the normal application identity, inserting a child for an existing parent succeeded and was rolled back; inserting a child for an absent parent failed with SQL Server error 547. No unchecked writes occurred afterward.
files.docs/cutover-runbook.md: Foreign-key gate: COMPLETE. Invoice row counts match, the constraint was enabled successfully, and invalid new writes are rejected. Open destination traffic after the other approved cutover gates.
